params.label: Stall width
params.where: Ch. D, Table 3 p.25; Table 9 p.35
params.note: Standard 90-degree stall width at service level 1 (pairs with a 5.80 m aisle).

params.label: Stall length
params.note: Minimum 90-degree stall length: 4.75 m design car + 0.25 m.

params.label: Aisle width (two-way)
params.where: Ch. D, Table 3 p.25; Sec. 13.3 p.60
params.note: Two-way aisle for 2.50 m stalls at service level 1.

params.label: Maximum ramp gradient
params.note: Maximum ramp gradient at service levels 1-2 (17% at level 3).

params.label: Ramp transition length
params.note: Each end of the ramp has a 3 m transition at half the gradient.

params.label: Floor-to-floor height
params.note: No Israeli figure found; MoT only gives 2.20 m clear height. US garages are typically 3.2-3.5 m floor to floor, per Purinton (2012).

params.label: Driving speed inside the lot
params.note: MoT design assumption for driving inside a parking facility (a design value, not a measurement). Shoup (2006) observed ~13 km/h while cruising on-street.

params.label: Fuel use at crawl speed
params.note: Measured idle consumption 0.279 cc/s = 1.0 L/h (2.5 L sedan); passenger cars 0.76-1.9 L/h. At crawl speed, consumption is modelled per hour, not per km.

params.label: CO₂ per litre of gasoline
params.note: 8,887 g CO2 per gallon of gasoline.

params.label: Gasoline price (95, self-service)
params.note: 95-octane self-service, October 2026, including VAT.

params.label: Value of travel time (non-work)
params.note: Value of travel time for non-work trips (2020 prices); parking search counts as travel time (p.115).

params.label: Mean parking duration
params.note: Mall garage: gamma-distributed stays with means 82.5-93.7 min.

params.label: Parking-duration shape (gamma)
params.note: Reported gamma shapes 1.12-2.53; mid-range value chosen.

params.label: Headline occupancy
params.note: Search effort becomes noticeable above ~85% occupancy and important above 92-93%.

params.label: Opening hours per day
params.note: Typical mall opening hours (10:00-22:00); only used to turn per-car savings into yearly totals.

params.label: Garage floors
params.note: Main scenario: a representative small multi-storey garage.

params.label: Aisles per floor
params.note: Parallel two-way aisles per floor, stalls on both sides, cross aisles at both ends.

params.label: Stalls per side of an aisle
params.note: 12 stalls per side = 30 m aisles; 3 floors x 3 aisles x 2 sides x 12 = 216 stalls.

params.label: Chance a searching driver notices a free stall (p)
params.note: Chance that a searching driver notices a free stall they pass. 1.0 = sees every one, the most favourable case for the driver, so the system's savings are a lower bound.

params.label: Reservation timeout (prototype)
params.note: Demo value. Real-world bound: farthest spot / search speed + parking manoeuvre margin.

benchmarks.note: Search effort becomes noticeable above ~85% occupancy.
Above 92-93% occupancy search exceeds 1 min (agent-based model, on-street).
At 95% occupancy search exceeds 2 min and over 5% of drivers fail.
Average search time off-street (30 s on-street); self-reported, n = 11,425.
Mean cruising from GPS ground truth, 3,000+ trips, Germany 2021-23 (abstract only).
Non-optimal cruising distance is 2.7x optimal in an open shopping-centre lot (abstract only).
Assignment with reservations cut average time-to-park by about half in simulation.
Space-availability information in zones cut search time by 16.2% (abstract only).
Smart parking in a university lot saved 11 s of search on average (abstract only).
Downtown on-street cruising, 16 studies 1927-2001 (not a garage baseline).
